what: A CDN keeps copies of your files on servers spread around the world, so people download them from somewhere close instead of from your own server every time.
like: Like a chain of corner shops stocking the same bread, so nobody has to drive to the bakery across town.
why: Pages and media load faster because the copy is near the user
Most requests never reach your origin, so it carries far less load and bandwidth
Absorbs traffic spikes and keeps serving while the origin is busy

steps.d: The request goes to a nearby edge server instead of your origin, so the round trip is short.
The edge builds a key from the URL (and any headers you choose) and checks whether it already holds that file.
If the copy is younger than its time to live (TTL), the edge answers straight away. That is a cache hit.
On a miss the edge asks a regional cache or your origin, stores the answer, then serves everyone nearby from that copy.
When you deploy, purge the old copy or use a new file name (app.v2.js), so users get the new version right away.

numbers.l: CloudFront's default TTL when you opt out of a cache policy
free invalidation paths per month on CloudFront
wins over max-age for shared caches like a CDN

choices.d: Long TTLs for files that never change (with a version in the name), short TTLs for pages that update. Use s-maxage to give the CDN a different time from browsers.

choices.t: What goes in the cache key
choices.d: Only what really changes the answer. Adding cookies or every header splits the cache into tiny pieces and the hit ratio drops.
Purging works for urgent fixes; versioned file names (app.3f2a.js) make deploys instant and need no purge at all.
stale-while-revalidate lets the edge answer with the old copy while it fetches the new one in the background, so nobody waits.

instead.why: Cache data your app computes, not whole files near users
The origin that stores the files the CDN serves
Spreads dynamic traffic across servers in one region

breaks.d: A long TTL keeps serving the previous version after a deploy.
breaks.see: Bug reports for something already fixed; old version in the response headers
breaks.fix: Versioned file names for assets, purge for pages, shorter TTL for HTML

breaks.d: The cache key includes things that vary per user, so almost every request is unique.
breaks.see: Hit ratio far below what you expect and origin traffic barely drops
breaks.fix: Strip cookies and unused query strings from the key; cache per user only when needed

breaks.d: A personalised page is stored in the shared cache and shown to someone else.
breaks.see: Users reporting someone else's name or cart
breaks.fix: Send Cache-Control: private or no-store on personal responses

breaks.d: Purging everything at once sends all requests to the origin together.
breaks.see: Origin CPU and errors spike right after a purge
breaks.fix: Purge only changed paths, use a regional shield, serve stale while refreshing

say: Static assets go behind a CDN with long TTLs and versioned file names, so deploys never wait for caches to expire.
I set s-maxage for the CDN and a shorter max-age for browsers, so I can purge the edge and still control freshness.
Personal responses are marked private, so the shared cache never stores them.
A regional shield in front of the origin means a cache miss in fifty cities becomes one request to us.

followups.q: How do you make sure users get a new version right after a deploy?
followups.a: Put a content hash in asset file names so every deploy creates new URLs, cache them for a long time, and keep the HTML on a short TTL or purge it on deploy.

followups.q: Can a CDN help dynamic, per-user pages?
followups.a: Yes, partly: it still terminates connections close to the user and keeps warm connections to the origin, and you can cache the shared parts while marking personal parts private.

followups.q: What is a good cache key?
followups.a: The URL plus only the headers or query parameters that change the response. Everything else should be stripped so similar requests share one cached copy.

check.q: Which header gives a CDN its own cache time, separate from browsers?
check.why: s-maxage applies to shared caches like a CDN and overrides max-age there.

check.q: You changed app.js but users still get the old one. The cleanest long-term fix?
check.a: Put a version or hash in the file name
d: Set the TTL to zero for everything
Turn the CDN off during deploys
check.why: A new name is a new URL, so caches fetch it fresh while old files stay cached safely.

check.q: A logged-in dashboard should never sit in the shared cache. What do you send?
check.why: private means only the user's own browser may store it.

check.q: Your hit ratio is very low. A likely cause?
check.a: Cookies or extra headers are part of the cache key
d: There are too many edge locations
check.why: Every distinct key is a separate cached copy, so per-user values make most requests unique.
